title: Case 426

plan.situation: Marisol Quang moved on 22 Sep and asked in writing that her full address never be shown to anyone but her. Order KF-88213 (AUD 214.50, paid on the card of C. Quang) was delivered to a Bicton Village locker and collected with the recipient code on 9 Oct 16:41. This morning a male caller, not on Marisol's number on file, left a voicemail claiming to be Marisol and asking for the address to be read back. Then Craig Quang emailed from an address that is not on file. He demands her address today and threatens a chargeback, a Consumer Protection complaint and a police report. He also makes claims about her health and their child. This looks like an attempt to locate a person who asked for her address to be protected. It goes to the supervisor, and nothing about her location is disclosed.

facts.fact: Marisol asked that her full address not be printed or shown anywhere a person other than her could see it; suburb only is acceptable
Profile updated; label setting is suburb + locker code only; notification email is still the shared household address marisol.craig.q@fastmail.example
Order KF-88213, AUD 214.50, card ending 5521, card holder C. Quang; confirmation went to the shared email
Delivered 2026-10-09 16:41 to the Bicton Village locker bank, locker 14, collected with the recipient code
The voicemail caller says he is Marisol but sounds male and is calling from a number that is not hers on file; he asks for the address to be read back
Craig Quang emails from craig.q.perth@outlook.example (not on file) demanding the address, with chargeback, Consumer Protection and police threats and claims about Marisol's health and the child
The voicemail and Craig's email probably come from the same person; the email mentions ringing this morning
The public tracking page shows suburb (Bicton) and the locker bank (Bicton Village) to anyone with the order number

conflicts: Event 005 caller says he is Marisol, but the voice is male and the number is not hers on file; Craig's email (event 006) says he rang this morning. The identity claim conflicts with the record. This goes to the supervisor; the desk does not decide who called.
missing_information: Whether Marisol has a safe contact channel other than the shared email (the phone number on file is hers, but whether contacting her is safe is for the supervisor to decide)
Whether Kestrel and Fern or Swan River Freight have already been contacted by Craig or given him anything
Whether the supervisor wants any welfare or police referral, based only on what the record shows
risk_flags: privacy_third_party: an unverified third party is asking for the address of a customer who explicitly asked for her address to be protected; possible domestic violence or stalking risk
Social engineering: the voicemail impersonates the account holder
Shared notification email gives the third party ongoing visibility of orders and delivery suburbs
Public tracking page shows the locker bank to anyone with the order number
Legal and chargeback threats are pressure, not new facts; they do not change who controls the address
Health and child claims about Marisol are unverified and must not be repeated to anyone

authority_map.controls: Her address and contact details and who may see them; her written instruction of 22 Sep stands
Only his own card dispute with his bank; no authority over the recipient's address
Whether and how to contact Marisol safely, the final wording of the reply to Craig, any welfare or police referral
Order notifications, the order record, disclosures from its own side
Public tracking display, label data, disclosures by its support staff

wait_check.new_since_last_promise: No promise has been made to Craig. New: impersonation voicemail (event 005) and an address demand from an unverified third party (event 006)

plan.decision_summary: Refuse to give out Marisol's address or locker, and send the decision to the supervisor (vulnerable person, impersonation, legal threats). Today, ask the merchant and carrier, sharing only what they need, not to disclose her delivery details and to stop sending notifications to the shared email.
plan.rationale: Marisol is the only person who controls her address, and she asked in writing that nobody else see it. The demand comes from an unverified sender and follows a voicemail impersonating her. That pattern and the possible risk to her safety mean the supervisor decides the reply and any contact with her or welfare referral. Two protective steps cannot wait: Craig can still see the shared notification email, and he could call the merchant or carrier, so both need to know about the restriction now. A reply to Craig is drafted in the handover for the supervisor to approve, so he still gets a clear next step today.

actions.purpose: Supervisor decides the reply to Craig, safe contact with Marisol and any referral
actions.subject: KF-88213 - third party demanding a protected customer's address; possible impersonation
actions.body: Handover, KF-88213 (Kestrel and Fern, AUD 214.50). On 22 Sep (event 001) account holder Marisol Quang asked in writing that her full address never be shown to anyone but her. Labels are set to suburb + locker only, but notifications still go to the shared household email marisol.craig.q@fastmail.example (event 002). Delivered and collected with the recipient code at the Bicton Village locker bank, 2026-10-09 16:41 AWST (event 004). Today 07:20 AWST: voicemail from +61 4xx xxx 906, caller says he is Marisol but sounds male and the number is not hers on file; he asks for the address to be read back (event 005). Today 10:02 AWST: Craig Quang, from craig.q.perth@outlook.example (not on file), demands the address, threatens chargeback, Consumer Protection and police, and makes unverified health and child claims (event 006). The public tracking page shows the Bicton Village locker bank to anyone with the order number (event 007). Nothing has been disclosed. The voicemail has not been returned. Decisions for you: (1) Approve or edit this draft reply to Craig, sent only to craig.q.perth@outlook.example and NOT the shared address: 'Dear Craig, thank you for your email about order KF-88213. We cannot share delivery addresses, delivery locations or account details with anyone other than the account holder, and we cannot discuss anyone's personal circumstances. Questions about a card payment should go to your card issuer. If you are worried about someone's safety, please contact WA Police on 131 444, or 000 in an emergency. Wattlebird Parcel Concierge.' (2) Whether and how to contact Marisol safely: not via the shared email; the phone on file is the only channel that may be hers. Offer to change her notification email, and say only that a third party asked about her order, nothing more. (3) Whether any welfare referral is warranted. Do not repeat Craig's claims. (4) If a chargeback arrives, handle it on the order record only, with no location data. Protective requests have been sent to Kestrel and Fern and to Swan River Freight (see actions).

actions.subject: KF-88213 - privacy restriction on customer details
actions.purpose: Stop location details leaking through the merchant's notifications or support staff
actions.body: Hello Kestrel and Fern team, about order KF-88213: the account holder has asked that her delivery address be kept private. Please (1) do not give the delivery address, suburb, locker or tracking details for this order or this customer to anyone who calls or emails, including anyone saying they paid for the order or belong to the household, and refer any such enquiry to Wattlebird Parcel Concierge; (2) stop sending order and shipping notifications for this customer to the email currently on file until we confirm a new contact with her directly; (3) let us know if anyone has already contacted you about this order since 1 October 2026. This is a request, not a confirmation of any change. Please confirm by reply today, 10 October 2026, before 17:00 AWST. Thank you, Hamish Reddaway, Wattlebird Parcel Concierge.

actions.subject: KF-88213 - restrict disclosure and public tracking detail
actions.purpose: Prevent the carrier disclosing the locker or address and reduce public tracking exposure
actions.body: Hello Swan River Freight team, about consignment KF-88213 (delivered 2026-10-09 16:41 AWST): the recipient has asked that her delivery details be kept private. Please (1) do not give the delivery address, locker bank, locker number or delivery details to any caller or emailer, including anyone saying they are the payer or a family member, and refer them to Wattlebird Parcel Concierge; (2) tell us whether the public tracking view for KF-88213 can be limited to status only, without the locker bank location; (3) confirm that the suburb + locker-only label setting stays on this recipient's profile; (4) tell us whether anyone has already contacted you about this consignment. This is a request, not a confirmation. Please reply today, 10 October 2026, before 17:00 AWST. Thank you, Hamish Reddaway, Wattlebird Parcel Concierge.

actions.purpose: Same-day check on supervisor decision and partner confirmations
actions.body: Check: is the supervisor's decision on the Craig reply and Marisol contact recorded; have Kestrel and Fern and Swan River Freight confirmed the restriction. If either partner has not replied, the supervisor follows up by phone. Make sure no reply goes to the shared household email.

not_doing: Not giving Craig or the voicemail caller any address, locker or confirmation that Marisol is a customer or where she lives; she controls this and has refused it in writing
Not returning the voicemail; the caller impersonated the account holder
Not emailing anything to the shared household address, which the third party can read
Not repeating or judging Craig's health or child claims, and not accusing anyone of anything
Not offering a refund or engaging with the chargeback threat; the card dispute is between Craig and his bank, and the threat does not change who controls the address
Not contacting Marisol directly before the supervisor decides how to do it safely
Not telling the merchant or carrier anything about personal circumstances; they get only the restriction
plan.follow_up: At 17:00 AWST on 10 Oct 2026: check the supervisor's decision (reply to Craig sent only after approval, safe contact with Marisol) and written confirmations from Kestrel and Fern and from Swan River Freight. If a partner is silent, the supervisor phones them. Any further contact from Craig or the 906 number goes straight to the supervisor with nothing disclosed.

review_rounds.plan_summary: Refuse to give out Marisol's address or locker, and send the decision to the supervisor (vulnerable person, impersonation, legal threats). Today, ask the merchant and carrier, sharing only what they need, not to disclose her delivery details and to stop sending notifications to the shared email.

issues.problem: The draft reply to Craig gives the WA Police numbers 131 444 and 000. These are correct public numbers, but they don't appear anywhere in the record.
issues.fix: Ask the supervisor to confirm the referral wording, or point to the official WA Police contact page instead of quoting numbers.

issues.problem: Asking the merchant to stop notifications to the shared email changes how Marisol is contacted without her direct instruction. Her 22 Sep request does reasonably cover it. Notifications stopping suddenly could also signal to the other reader of that inbox that something has changed.
issues.fix: Keep the request, but mark it in the handover as something the supervisor should confirm with Marisol when she is contacted safely.

issues.problem: Some case_parameters don't match the plan: urgency is 'none' and queue is 'carrier_ops', but the plan escalates as urgent to the supervisor over a possible safety risk.
issues.fix: Set urgency to high and the queue to supervisor/trust-and-safety.

review.summary: This is a strong plan. It refuses to disclose anything and does not return the impersonation voicemail. It escalates the reply to Craig and any contact with Marisol to the supervisor. It sends the merchant and carrier the minimum they need to stop disclosure, without passing on Craig's claims, and keeps the shared email out of it. Only minor grounding and parameter issues remain.
